data: Welcome to the documentation for pd (go-pixeldrain), a fast and versatile command-line interface, Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, and Go SDK for Pixeldrain.
data.key-capabilities#Key Capabilities: Command Line Interface (pd): Upload, download, create albums, and manage files without touching a web browser. Model Context Protocol (pd mcp): Seamlessly connect Pixeldrain file capabilities to AI agents (Claude Desktop, Cursor, etc.). End-to-End Encryption: Encrypt files client-side before sending them to the cloud using age or SSH keys. Unix Pipelines: Native support for stdin, stdout, and tar streaming. Go SDK: Programmatic access to the Pixeldrain REST API v2 in Go applications.
data.overview#Overview: Pixeldrain is a reliable and fast file-sharing and cloud storage service. pd brings the full power of Pixeldrain into your terminal, scripts, and AI workflows.
data.table-of-contents#Table of Contents: Quick Start: Learn how to install pd and start sharing files immediately. MCP Server (AI Integration): Configure AI agents to transfer files through Pixeldrain. End-to-End Encryption: Encrypt your uploads client-side for maximum confidentiality. Go SDK: Use go-pixeldrain as a library in your Go projects.

data:
pd provides built-in End-to-End Encryption (E2EE) using the modern age encryption tool or your existing SSH public keys.
All encryption and decryption happen strictly on your machine before uploading or after downloading. Pixeldrain only ever sees encrypted bytes.
data.decrypting-downloads#Decrypting Download:
To download and decrypt the file automatically, pass your private identity file with --identity:
pd download --identity ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 https://pixeldrain.com/u/xxxxxx
data.multiple-recipients#Multiple Recipients:
Encrypt a file for multiple recipients listed in a file (one recipient key per line):
pd upload --recipient-file recipients.txt confidential.pdf
data.using-an-age-public-key-or-ssh-public-ke:
Encrypt a file for a specific recipient:
# Encrypt with an age recipient key pd upload --recipient "age1ql3z7hjy54pw3hyww5ayyfg7zqgvc7w3j2elw8zmrj2kg5sfn9aqmcac8p" confidential.pdf # Encrypt with an SSH public key pd upload --recipient "ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAI... user@example.com" confidential.pdf Uploaded files will automatically be saved with the .age extension appended.

data: pd comes with a built-in Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, allowing AI agents like Claude Desktop, Cursor, and custom LLM workflows to interact with Pixeldrain.
data.available-mcp-tools#Available MCP Tools:
The pd mcp server exposes the following tools:
Tool Description upload_files Uploads one or more base64-encoded files (images, audio, zip archives) and returns a file or album URL. upload_text Uploads text or markdown content as a file and returns the shareable link. download_file Downloads a file from Pixeldrain to the specified local path. With these tools, AI assistants can easily create sharable links for generated artifacts, charts, or images, as well as fetch remote assets during interactive sessions.
data.claude-desktop#Claude Desktop:
Add the following to your claude_desktop_config.json (~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json on macOS):
{ "mcpServers": { "pixeldrain": { "command": "pd", "args": ["mcp"], "env": { "PIXELDRAIN_API_KEY": "your_api_key_here" } } } } Note PIXELDRAIN_API_KEY is optional. If provided, uploads will be associated with your Pixeldrain account.
data.cursor--other-mcp-clients#Cursor / Other: Configure the command as pd and arguments as ["mcp"].
data.starting-the-mcp-server#Starting the MCP:
Start the stdio-based MCP server with:
pd mcp

data: Learn how to install and use the pd CLI for day-to-day file transfers, album creation, and pipelines.
data.authentication-optional#Authentication (:
pd works anonymously out-of-the-box. However, if you have a Pixeldrain account, configuring your API key allows you to manage files under your user account and keep track of your uploads.
Get your API key at pixeldrain.com/user/api_keys.
You can supply the API key in either of two ways:
Environment Variable (Recommended):
export PIXELDRAIN_API_KEY="your-api-key" Command Flag:
pd --api-key "your-api-key" upload file.zip
data.binary-releases#Binary Releases: Download pre-compiled binaries for macOS, Linux, or Windows from the GitHub Releases page.
data.create-albums#Create Albums:
Combine multiple files into a single album URL using --album:
pd upload --album "Neon Dreams" concept1.png concept2.png concept3.png # => https://pixeldrain.com/l/xxxxxx
data.download-files#Download Files:
Download a file by URL or ID (saved to current directory by default):
pd download https://pixeldrain.com/u/xxxxxx Specify a custom destination directory or filename:
pd download -o ./downloads https://pixeldrain.com/u/xxxxxx pd download --filename custom.png https://pixeldrain.com/u/xxxxxx To download all files from an album non-interactively:
pd download --all https://pixeldrain.com/l/xxxxxx
data.go-install#Go Install:
If you have Go installed (Go 1.24 or later recommended):
go install github.com/jkawamoto/go-pixeldrain/cmd/pd@latest
data.homebrew-macos--linux#Homebrew (macOS \u:
The easiest way to install pd on macOS or Linux is via Homebrew:
brew tap jkawamoto/pixeldrain brew install pixeldrain
data.upload-files#Upload Files:
To upload a file and print the public link:
pd upload artwork.png # => https://pixeldrain.com/u/xxxxxx To specify a custom display name on Pixeldrain using path:name:
pd upload output_0042.png:cyberpunk-city.png
data.uploading-entire-directories#Uploading E:
Stream directory archives directly to Pixeldrain without intermediate disk writes:
tar zcf - ~/Projects/my-app | pd upload -- -:my-app.tar.gz And download/extract in a single pipeline:
pd download | tar zxf - -C ~/Downloads
data.uploading-from-stdin#Uploading from STDI:
Upload log files, git diffs, or output from any program by providing - as the path (use -- before - so flags aren’t confused):
# Upload build logs cat build.log | pd upload -- -:build.log # Upload a git patch git diff | pd upload -- -:patch.diff

data: go-pixeldrain is also a full-featured Go client library for the Pixeldrain REST API.
data.documentation--api-reference#Documentati: Full Go package documentation and API references are hosted on pkg.go.dev/github.com/jkawamoto/go-pixeldrain. Source code and examples are available on GitHub.
data.installation#Installation:
Add the library to your Go module:
go get github.com/jkawamoto/go-pixeldrain
